quest.title: Go to the Institute Dormitories and retrieve the Anchor
quest.description: You arrived at the new Fontaine Research Institute and met with co-administrators Raimondo and Choiseul. After a long, mind-numbing conversation, you were tasked to escort Nacker and retrieve the last two Anchors.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x25000

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Is this where researchers spent their downtime? Is this even humane? Has the Fontaine Research Institute ever considered making renovating this place a priority?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: ...There should be a Survey Anchor here. Just like Ms. Chronie implied, this place needs renovation, and the power supply here is very limited... Or perhaps I should say, there's a complete shortage.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: #While I'm answering Ms. Chronie's questions, I'll leave the job of recovering the Survey Anchor to you, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Compared to some other areas, the dormitories weren't impacted as much by the explosion.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Dormitories? But I don't see even one bed here, so how do the researchers get any rest? It's not like they can sleep in chairs, right?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Ms. Chronie, your idea of "resting" is very different from that of the researchers.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: When a researcher at the Fontaine Research Institute says they need rest, they only want a quick break for their brain.

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Then, they would usually come here, play piano, read, and have a drink or two if necessary.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Uh, but wouldn't sleeping provide more rest for the brain?

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: You may be correct, but... To our researchers, sleeping is a waste of time in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Chronie
dialogues.text: Sleeping is a waste of time? No, it is essential for rest!

dialogues.speaker: Nacker
dialogues.text: Sleeping completely cuts your train of thought short, and that's just not acceptable for our research work.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Are you being serious? If you don't sleep, the only thing that'll be cut short is your life!

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Not necessarily. The institute boasts an excellent health care system that guarantees researchers' health and well-being.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: But that's still no reason to not sleep!

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: Also, if researchers are here to give their brains a break, wouldn't that break their thought process from research, anyway?

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Not necessarily. It only seems like they're taking a break when actually, they're still pondering different academic subjects subconsciously.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: It's akin to a vast ocean that, while appearing calm on the surface, still has a strong undercurrent beneath.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Sometimes, the undercurrents below are much stronger than the towering waves above.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: I get it. You mean when researchers of the Fontaine Research Institute are on a project, they must keep working and are not allowed to rest, right?

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: That is not completely fair to say. If they truly need sleep, they're free to go back home and do just that.

response.speaker: Chronie
response.text: So, it is fairer to say that as long as researchers of the Fontaine Research Institute are inside the Institute, they must keep working and are not allowed to rest.

response.speaker: Nacker
response.text: Your rhetoric is simply astound, Ms. Chronie.
